title: Cost, Visas Shape Students' Study-Abroad Choices
paragraphs: Every year, millions of students leave their home countries to study abroad, hoping to maybe experience a new culture, meet new people and create opportunities for their future.
But how do these students choose where to go?

To find out, Navitas, an Australian education services company, surveyed 870 education agents in 64 countries. These agents help students choose where to study, and also help them apply to universities and prepare to study abroad.
The survey asked about the factors influencing students' choices of where to study.

And across all regions of the world, the most important factor was cost — both the costs of university fees, and the cost of living. This was named by 82% of agents as one of the top factors influencing students' choices.
Globally, the next most important factor, named by 61% of agents, was access to post-study work opportunities.
The third-most-important factor was education quality, followed by safety.

However, things were a little different in Africa, where the third-most-important factor was the ability to get a visa. This was also the fourth-most-important factor in South Asia, after access to work while studying.
And visas were a worry for many — 86% of agents said their clients were "concerned" or "very concerned" about the risk of sudden changes to visa rules. Only the cost of living worried students more.

In fact, 80% of agents said lower visa acceptance rates can discourage some of the strongest students from applying to a university abroad. And 76% said students with good grades and enough money to study abroad are more likely to choose countries where they have a better chance of getting a visa.

As for which countries students are most attracted to lately, the country seeing the most positive change was New Zealand. Eighty-eight percent of agents agreed that its reputation for being both "safe" and "welcoming" has improved, while 80% said they had seen more interest in studying there over the previous two months.
